steps.description: Read /eval-phase0-without-two-group-n3-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 x 7; first column gene symbol, 6 sample count columns) and /eval-phase0-without-two-group-n3-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (6 x 2, one row per sample with a condition column). steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between the drug-treated and control liver samples, at what fold change and FDR?
constraints: Model raw integer counts — never log-transformed or CPM values — with the NB GLM
Set the control group as the reference level so positive log2FC means up in treated
Use BH FDR across all tested genes; do not report nominal p-values as significant
Report shrunken log2FC for ranking but the unshrunken estimate alongside it
The p-value histogram must be produced and its shape commented on (uniform-with-spike vs conservative vs anti-conservative)
Do not filter to a hand-picked gene list at any point
State the engine actually used and its version in the output
steps.description: Run negative-binomial differential expression on the filtered raw counts from T1S1, contrasting treated vs control using the condition column of metadata.csv, with control as the reference level. Preferred engine: DESeq2 (design ~ condition, Wald test, independent filtering on, BH adjustment, plus lfcShrink with apeglm or ashr for ranking). Report the full result table for every tested gene — gene symbol, baseMean, raw log2FC, shrunken log2FC, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj — sorted by padj, written to CSV. Summarise: number of genes with padj < 0.05, padj < 0.1, and the subset of those with |log2FC| > 1; split into up- and down-regulated. steps.name: Power, stability and permutation audit of the 3v3 design
caveats: Post-hoc power computed from the observed dispersions is descriptive, not a substitute for a prospective power calculation
Leave-one-out with n=3 produces 2v3 comparisons whose dispersion estimates are even weaker — interpret overlap as a stability probe, not a validation
With only 10 possible label assignments the permutation null is coarse; treat it as an order-of-magnitude check on the false-positive load
steps.context: This step is the direct answer to the second half of the research question. It uses the same filtered counts (T1S1) and the same model and result table (T1S2) so the comparison is like-for-like.
steps.question: How much confidence do three replicates per group support — what effect size is detectable, how stable is the top gene ranking to dropping one replicate, and how many hits survive a label permutation null?
constraints: Reuse the exact filtering, normalisation and test used in T1S2 for every leave-one-out and permuted run — no re-tuning
Enumerate permutations exhaustively; do not sample randomly from only 10 possible splits
Report power as a function of both fold change and mean expression, not a single number
Do not present the leave-one-out stable core as an independently validated gene set — it is the same data reused
Fix and record the random seed for any simulation
steps.description: Quantify the statistical confidence of the T1S2 result using this dataset's own dispersions rather than generic rules of thumb. (a) Summarise the fitted per-gene dispersion distribution from T1S2 across expression deciles, and report the typical biological coefficient of variation. (b) Post-hoc power: for a grid of log2 fold changes (0.5, 1, 1.5, 2) and mean expression levels spanning the observed range, compute the power of the 3v3 NB test at the achieved FDR, either analytically or by simulating counts from the fitted mean-dispersion relationship; report the minimum detectable log2FC at 80% power for a typically expressed gene. (c) Replicate stability: repeat the differential expression six times, each time leaving out one of the six samples (2v3 or 3v2), and report the overlap of the top 100 genes and of the padj<0.05 set with the full-data result — a Jaccard summary plus the count of hits that survive all six leave-one-out runs. Label the latter as the stable core. (d) Permutation null: enumerate the distinct treated/control label assignments for 6 samples (10 distinct 3v3 splits, 3 non-trivial beyond the true one and its complement), rerun the same test under each, and report the number of genes reaching padj<0.05 under permuted labels versus true labels. State explicitly that with 3v3 the exact permutation p-value has a floor of ~0.1, so no gene can be individually significant by a non-parametric test — this bounds what the parametric result is really claiming. Write a single confidence assessment table and a plain-language verdict on which findings are robust and which are provisional.
acceptance_criteria: Minimum detectable log2FC at 80% power is reported for at least one representative expression level, with the dispersion assumption stated
Leave-one-out overlap statistics for all six runs are reported, and the stable-core gene set is written to CSV
Number of padj<0.05 genes under each permuted labelling is reported alongside the true labelling
The exact-permutation p-value floor for a 3v3 design is stated explicitly
A written confidence verdict distinguishes robust from provisional findings

caveats: Enrichment inherits every weakness of the underlying DE result — a pathway called from an unstable gene set is itself unstable
ORA on a small significant set is badly underpowered and its p-values should be treated as descriptive

steps.context: Human liver, drug treatment. Pathway-level aggregation borrows strength across genes and is the appropriate resolution when only 3 replicates per group are available.
steps.question: Which biological processes and pathways are coordinately shifted in the drug-treated liver samples, given that per-gene power at n=3 is limited?
constraints: Use human gene sets only — the data is Homo sapiens, taxon 9606
Use the filtered gene universe from T1S1 as the ORA background
Run the rank-based test on all tested genes, not only the significant ones
Report negative results for the pre-specified liver/xenobiotic pathway families explicitly
If no gene set resource is present, report that and stop the step cleanly with the ranked list as output — do not substitute an improvised gene set
steps.description: Interpret the T1S2 differential expression result at pathway resolution, which is where a weak per-gene signal can still be read. Run two complementary analyses on the human gene symbols in the result table: (1) over-representation analysis on the padj<0.05 set (and, if that set is small, on the padj<0.1 set, clearly labelled), tested against the background of all genes that passed filtering in T1S1 — not against the whole genome; (2) a rank-based gene set test (GSEA-style or a competitive test such as CAMERA/fgsea) using every tested gene ranked by shrunken log2FC or the signed test statistic, which does not require a significance cutoff and is therefore the more informative of the two at this sample size. Given the liver tissue and drug-treatment context, explicitly check the direction and significance of xenobiotic/drug-metabolism, nuclear-receptor (e.g. AhR, CAR, PXR, PPAR), oxidative-stress/NRF2, bile-acid, lipid-metabolism and inflammatory/acute-phase gene sets, and report them whether or not they reach FDR significance rather than reporting only what is positive. acceptance_criteria: Both ORA and a rank-based gene set test are attempted, or their absence is explained by a named missing resource
Enrichment results with FDR, set size and leading-edge genes are written to CSV
The pre-specified liver drug-response pathway families are reported with their statistics regardless of significance
The gene set collection actually used, including its version if recorded, is named in the output

plan.title: Liver drug-treated vs control DE (n=3) + power audit
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single-batch bulk RNA-seq experiment in human liver: a 12,000 gene x 7 column Salmon count matrix (counts.csv, first column gene symbol, 6 sample columns) and a 6 x 2 sample table (metadata.csv, one row per sample with a condition column) encoding 3 drug-treated vs 3 control samples, unpaired. The research question has two halves and the plan mirrors them.

Track 1 answers 'which genes are differentially expressed'. T1S1 loads and reconciles the two CSVs, checks that sample identifiers match between counts and metadata, filters low-count genes, applies a variance-stabilising transform and runs unsupervised QC (library sizes, per-sample detected genes, PCA, sample-sample correlation) to establish that the treated/control split is the dominant structure and that no sample is an outlier — with n=3 a single aberrant replicate can drive the entire result, so this must be established before, not after, the contrast. T1S2 runs the actual differential expression with a negative-binomial GLM on raw counts (DESeq2 if importable, edgeR quasi-likelihood or limma-voom as fallbacks, pyDESeq2 if only Python is present), contrasting treated vs control, with independent filtering, BH FDR and shrunken log fold changes for ranking. The estimated dispersion trend and the raw p-value histogram are required outputs because they are the honest diagnostic for whether the NB fit is trustworthy at three replicates.

Track 2 answers 'how confident can we be with three replicates'. This is the part most analyses skip, and with n=3 it is not optional. T2S1 quantifies the confidence directly from this dataset rather than from a textbook: per-gene dispersion distribution, the resulting detectable-effect-size floor across the expression range, a post-hoc power curve over log2 fold change and mean expression, leave-one-out replicate stability of the top gene ranking, and a permutation/label-reshuffle null showing how many 'significant' genes arise under all three possible non-trivial relabellings — with 3v3 there are only 10 distinct label assignments, so the exact permutation p-value floor is 0.1 per gene, which is itself the key statement about what a 3v3 design can and cannot support. T2S2 takes the DE result forward to pathway-level interpretation, which is the appropriate resolution when per-gene power is low: over-representation on the FDR-significant set plus a rank-based gene set test using the full shrunken-LFC ranking, so that a weak per-gene signal can still be read at the pathway level. Gene sets are reference data (a human pathway/GO collection); the reference store currently reports as unprovisioned, so T2S2 must confirm what it holds at run time and, if no gene set collection and no annotation package is available, report that plainly and return only the ranked list rather than substituting a hand-written set. That loss costs an annotation layer, not the answer to the research question, so the plan proceeds rather than blocking.

The package inventory could not be read, so no step may assume a library. Every step probes its imports first and degrades along a named fallback chain, and each step writes its DE/statistical results as plain CSV so downstream steps are not coupled to whichever engine succeeded.
